posts.caption:
Fewer new buildings were supposed to mean fewer empty units.
The latest Census numbers say not yet.

U.S. rental vacancy was 7.6% in the third quarter, up from 7.3% in the second quarter and 7.1% a year ago. That came even as apartment completions through September ran 27% below last year, per RealPage, though third quarter deliveries did tick up from the second.

Here in the West, rental vacancy rose to 6.7% from 6.0% a year earlier. Phoenix was among the five metros RealPage named for the most third quarter deliveries, each above 3,000 units, and Apartment List shows the median rent in the city of Phoenix down 2.5% over the past 12 months.

In my experience, a construction slowdown rarely fixes leasing on its own. The units that delivered this year and last still have to fill, and renters may have more options than they did.

So before anyone decides the pressure is easing, I would want one answer at each property: is our vacancy coming from fewer renters finding us, or from more choices near us? Those call for very different responses.

Which one are you seeing in Arizona right now?

#Multifamily #PropertyManagement #ArizonaRealEstate

posts.caption:
A vacancy rate is a count of empty units.
It is also a count of the choices a renter has.

When more units sit open, the comparison starts earlier. Much of that comparing may happen on maps, review sites and listings, and a community can be ruled out there on trust before a renter ever reaches out.

The Census Bureau put rental vacancy in the West at 6.7% last quarter, up from 6.0% a year earlier. We read that less as a pricing story and more as a discovery story. More choice may raise the bar for being found and trusted, not only for being cheapest.

That changes where marketing effort pays off: replies to reviews that show how the team handles a problem; a map presence that looks cared for; and a clear answer to why here instead of the place down the street.

When renters have more options, what is the first thing that gets a community ruled out?

#Multifamily #ApartmentMarketing #PropTech

posts.caption:
Vacancy is up nationally.
Here is how a property team can tell whether it is showing up locally.

The Census Bureau reported U.S. rental vacancy at 7.6% in Q3 2026 and 6.7% in the West, both higher than a year earlier. A regional number is a prompt to look closer, not a reason to change pricing on its own.

Five things worth reviewing before responding:
1. Leads per vacant unit: is demand down, or is the same demand spread across more units?
2. Days vacant by floor plan: is the pressure property wide, or in one unit type?
3. Tour to lease conversion: are renters visiting and then choosing somewhere else?
4. Nearby comps: are asking rents and specials moving at the communities renters compare you with?
5. Renewals: are current residents staying at the rate the budget assumes?

If leads are steady but conversion is slipping, the answer may sit in the experience. If leads are falling, start with how the community gets found.

#Multifamily #PropertyManagement #PillarCommunities

posts.caption:
More empty rentals means more comparing.
And much of it may happen before anyone calls you.

The Census Bureau put U.S. rental vacancy at 7.6% last quarter, up from 7.1% a year earlier. In plain words, roughly 1 in 13 rental homes was empty and for rent.

As a marketer, I read that as a shift in leverage. When a renter has more options, the first cut may happen quietly on a phone, and it may never show up in your lead reports.

That is the gap between being seen and being chosen. Being seen gets you into the comparison. Being chosen depends on whether you answered the renter's questions before they had to ask.

Three checks for the floor plan you most need to lease:
1. Does it have its own photos and layout online, or only the model?
2. Send an inquiry from your own website after 6 PM. How long until a real reply?
3. Can a renter see a starting price for it without calling?

If one of those misses, you may be losing renters you never knew were looking.

Which of the three would surprise your team most?

#Multifamily #ApartmentMarketing #AISearch
